title: Central Nervous
System Anomalies
Rehabilitation
hero.text: For children affected by neurological and developmental conditions, to help manage symptoms, support development and improve quality of life

overview: The central nervous system (CNS), primarily the brain and spinal cord, underpins nearly every process in a child’s body, from movement and sensation to thought, memory and awareness. In newborns it is still developing, and anomalies can arise that affect development or lead to long-term complications. Our paediatric CNS rehabilitation programme supports children living with these conditions, whether congenital or acquired, providing early, expert and long-term care designed to reduce symptoms, support development and improve quality of life.

topics.label: What Is Central Nervous System Anomalies Rehabilitation

blocks.text: Central nervous system anomalies rehabilitation at Cambridge Hospital is a specialised paediatric programme that supports children whose brain or spinal cord development has been affected by congenital conditions, illness, or injury.
Our team provides expert, familycentred care that helps children build strength, improve function and achieve important developmental milestones.
We care for children with a range of congenital and acquired central nervous system conditions, affecting either the spinal cord or the brain, including but not limited to:

items: Effects of traumatic brain or spinal cord injury.

blocks.text: A physiatrist (a physical medicine and rehabilitation physician) typically leads the process, carrying out a full assessment, considering the child’s symptoms, and ordering appropriate tests before designing an individualised plan.
The child’s age is always a priority, since options suitable for newborns are more limited than those for older children. Care usually combines several methods over the long term:

items: **Inpatient rehabilitation -** the child is admitted for treatment and rehabilitation; for more severe anomalies this includes 24/7 monitoring by nursing staff experienced in caring for infants and toddlers and skilled at identifying emerging issues early
**Physiotherapy for babies, and occupational therapy and related strategies for older children** - to support recovery and develop functional abilities
**Recovery support after surgery** - where a procedure has been needed, rehabilitation supports the child’s recovery and helps restore function
**A home programme** - many children return home, where therapists guide parents through specific exercises and activities, with regular check-ups and scheduled therapy sessions throughout.

blocks.text: A healthy central nervous system supports better learning, thinking and awareness, while anomalies can interfere with early development and sometimes have effects that persist beyond childhood.
Beginning rehabilitation at the time of diagnosis allows for early treatment, and a continuous programme of care and support can help improve a child’s quality of life and overall functioning.
